name: IGAC
body: A declared language, a permanent https redirect, dates on its pages, and content shaped as questions and answers. But the home page still carries a Universal Analytics tag, which Google stopped processing in July 2024.
lesson: Remove retired UA- tags and keep the GA4 one. Dead tags add weight, collect nothing, and confuse audits.
summary: www.igac.gov.co scores 66 out of 100 (D). 3 checks fail now, 29 are at risk, and 14 pass. Fix first: 1 internal link leads to an error.

fix.title: 1 internal link leads to an error
fix.fix: Fix or remove each link, or redirect the old address with a 301 to the closest live page.

fix.title: Some pages are closed to AI answer crawlers
fix.evidence: OAI-SearchBot cannot read 1 page, ChatGPT-User cannot read 1 page, Claude-SearchBot cannot read 1 page, Claude-User cannot read 1 page.
fix.fix: Check that the closed paths are meant to stay out of AI answers.

fix.title: 19 pages have no meta description
fix.evidence: /, /user/login, /index.php/, /index.php/el-igac and 15 more. Google and AI answers then write their own snippet from whatever text they find.
fix.fix: Write a 50 to 160 character description for each page that says what a reader gets.

fix.title: No content security policy
fix.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 19 pages analyzed. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
fix.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

fix.title: 5 cookies are sent without Secure
fix.evidence: Without Secure: __uzma, __uzmb, __uzme, __uzmc and 1 more. Set on /, /user/login, /index.php/ and 16 more.
fix.fix: Set Secure on every cookie, and HttpOnly plus SameSite=Lax on session cookies.

fix.title: Universal Analytics code is still on the page
fix.evidence: Google stopped processing Universal Analytics data in July 2024. The code adds weight and collects nothing.
fix.fix: Remove the UA- tag and keep GA4.

works.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http redirects permanently to https
The start page declares its language
The start page sets a mobile viewport
The start page reads well without JavaScript
